text: This is my favorite park in Tucson besides Reid Park. First of all, it is a huge park. It comprises two little lakes, a dog park, a very large green area, and equally big sandy walking areas. Walking alongside the lakes is also nice. The ground there is sandy but it is still very pretty. There are many trees all over the park, which adds to the beauty of the park and also provides shade when you need to take a break. There are trash cans and drinking fountains all over as well and everything is very clean and well-maintained. The dog park is great as well. It is divided into a small park (for small dogs, I suppose) and a bigger park. The small park is just dirt but the bigger park has a grassy area. There are benches and some trees for shade. There is a water hose and a tub, so you can clean your dog if the dog got dirty, which I find super convenient! Also, some people left toys there, so you don't even need to bring your own toys. You can just play with the ones that are already there. The crowd that comes here is mostly people fishing in the lake and people walking their dogs. A lot of the dog walkers are people volunteering at the dog shelter that is close by. They take the shelter dogs for a walk. So be prepared to meet many dogs when you come here. However, the shelter dogs seem to actually be some of the more well-behaved dogs. In general, there is never any problem. Everyone just peacefully walks their dogs. In addition to fishers and dog walkers, there are sometimes people flying their model airplanes or playing with their model motorboats. The motorboats are very loud, so that can be a little annoying. Speaking of noises, sometimes you can hear the dogs from the shelter nearby barking. I personally don't mind and my dog just ignores it but if that is something that bothers you, this park might not be ideal for you. All in all, this is a really great park. I love coming here.

text: I watched Sean Brock on Mind of a Chef and that's how I found out about the restaurant. I love his passion for souther food, and not just the butter and fried parts, but the vegetables and grains. I was surprised to find that he has a second restaurant in Nashville and was super excited to try out the food when I was in town for the weekend. Normally I would never order a vegetarian dish, but knowing the chef's focus on more rural southern cuisine that's more vegetable and grain based, I had to order the vegetable plate. Surprisingly, it was the most expensive item on the brunch menu, and you could never go wrong ordering the most expensive item ;). We started out with pimento cheese. I never had it before and enjoyed the sharp flavors. I wasn't a big fan of the chips that came with the dish, some were a bit stale, but the cheese spread went splendidly with the lovely fresh dinner rolls. Was happy that I could knock that item off of my list of southern specialty foods. The vegetable plate consisted of 4 items, a radish salad, grits with braised greens and soft egg, cabbage and mushrooms and wheat berries. Being the little peasant at heart, I devoured the cabbage. I'm not ashamed to say it, but that was my favorite item for the meal. They layered the cabbage with different levels of doneness, with raw cabbage at the bottom, sautéed cabbages in the middle and braised cabbage at the top. They used very little spices so the sweetness of the cabbage really came through. What an art form to elevate the humble cabbage to such exalted levels. The grits were pretty good, although it didn't have enough textural differences in the dish to make it stand out. I liked the radish salad quite a bit, too. The winter is great for cabbage and radish, bearing extra sweet produce. I didn't like the wheat berries and mushrooms all that much. It was too salty and there was a sourness in the dish that didn't sit well with me. We got the sorghum pie for dessert. I was hoping they had a sweet potato or buttermilk pie but no luck. I didn't like the sorghum pie. It's not everyone's cup of tea. The heavy molasses taste was a bit much for me. Wish they used something else to cut the flavor. The crust was also super dense and not flakey. If I'm ever back in Nashville or in charleston, I'll make sure to plan ahead more and get dinner reservations. Our service was impeccable and I loved the decor and ambiance of the restaurant. Would make a lovely date spot the prices are super reasonable, too.

The stuffed pizzas only come in large but should probably considered a double-large. As the name would suggest, the toppings are stuffed between two crusts. The top crust seemed to be dusted with garlic, oil and parmesan cheese adding an extra magic to the pie. There was a great Italian flavor with each bite. Even the broccoli rabe tasted fresh and nicely seasoned. Despite two layers of crust and a large amount of fillings, it was still manageable to pick up or cut with a knife and fork. Unfortunately, I didn't love the eggplant parm sandwich which I also ordered and will be deducting a star from my review. It wasn't well breaded and the eggplant was just of ok quality. The sauce, cheese bread and eggplant didn't blend together as an eggplant parmesan sandwich should. Eggplant parm sandwiches are a dime a dozen in Philly, but the stuffed pizza was so amazing and unique that I won't let the sandwich get me down. Between the sandwiches and pizza, we had leftovers. The pizza tasted awesome hot & fresh, but then amazing cold out of the fridge. We ordered through Grubhub and the delivery came within about an hour on a Friday night. The prices were also reasonable. Luigi's Pizza Fresca definitely left its impression on me and I can't wait to order their stuffed pizza again.

The last two concerts I saw here, the sound kept cutting in and out of one of the PA systems which was totally annoying. It reminded me of the time I had a bad speaker in my car which cut in and out whenever I hit a bump. The security and usher staff at The Venue are always friendly and jovial. The barcode scanners that they use to scan tickets at the door never work properly and they always have a clever one-liner to spout off about how unreliable modern technology is. The absolute worst thing about this place is the seating. The Venue's seating plan consists of around two thousand metal folding chairs all zip-tied together. It's bad enough that the chairs are cheap and uncomfortable but zap-strapping them together just makes it ten times worse because they're simply too close together. It looks like a concert hall that caters to anorexics and bulimics only - and I'm a skinny guy, so that's saying a lot. Prepare to spend an intimate evening with your neighbour rubbing your thighs and elbows together. I understand that the Venue probably does this to keep the chairs organized in their rows and to keep people from tossing them in the air when their ass gets too sore to sit any longer but there has to be a better way to secure the chairs than this. When purchasing tickets I always try to get a seat at the end of the aisle so I at least have breathing room on one side of me. The seats aren't numbered either which makes it even more fun to find your chair if you're seated in the middle of the row. You'll have to count your way in. There's only two sets of small doors to get in and out of the Venue, both located at the back of the structure. These doors lead to a sharp ninety-degree turn into an incredibly narrow hallway which brings you back into the casino. If there's ever a fire in this concert hall it is going to be an absolute nightmare to get out of there. Imagine two thousand people rushing for those two small doors and that small hallway at the same time? I hope The Venue has better plan for fire evacuation than they do for seating. Great White are playing here in a couple of months so I guess I'll find out then. (Was that tasteless?) Other than the seats, the Venue is actually quite spacious to move around in. Lots of room between the back rows to get to the beer line and the merchandise counter. I think the building needs a separate entrance and exit but being that it's part of a casino, that will never happen. How will they get people to gamble if they don't have to move through the casino to get to the concert?

The hostess then tells us to wait and they'll make us up a table in the dining room. We wait 5 minutes and watch a handful of staff debate what to do with us while glancing at their watches. Resto closes at 10 so we figure we've become the pain in the ass rezo keeping everyone from leaving work early on a Sunday night. Sorry about that. Five minutes later the hostess returns to tell us the dining room is closed. We're hungry, so we accept we're having our steak dinners in a lame sports bar / lounge. The young waitress comes up to our table, vocal frys us and we decide to go with a dozen of the buck a shucks we figured out were the "All Night Sunday" special. Waitress tells us the deal ended at 630. Chalkboard says "All Night Sunday" but we're not looking for a fight so we say nothing. I order a rib eye rare, it shows up medium rare. First world problems. As far as steakhouses go, you're better off at the Keg b/c at least the Keg isn't pretending to be anything more than what it is. You want a real steak cooked by someone who actually gives a F, go somewhere else and pay the extra dough. On the upside, the bill was pretty cheap for a steak. This place is a wannabe player in a game it's never played.

The shrimp cocktail was quite disappointing. 5 "30-35 shrimp" as I call them (you can get 30-35, frozen per pound - not big at all) in a glass on limp wilted lettuce served with decent cocktail sauce... Think Heinz cocktail with a bit of pace picante... Seriously, I think that might be what it was. 20+ minutes. Seriously. This is ridiculous. Not that it matters, but I'll talk about the entrees anyway, just to complete the review, and I will be fair.... Wait! It gets better! Our server just informed me... Almost an HOUR AFTER I ORDERED that they ARE ALL OUT OF WHAT I ORDERED!!! The Halibut and chips my wife ordered were good. The Halibut was thin, but very tasty. The sauce to dip the halibut was a nice compliment to a perfect batter. Fries were great, perfectly fried. We shared it, cause I am soooo very hungry. Off to Carl's Jr where I will get decent food incredibly fast at a fair price. Damn it, I wanted to love this place. Never to return.

So disappointed in this place and the people who flock here claiming how wonderful the food is. Again, I am concerned we Americans have lost touch with what good food is supposed to be. Pretty sure this place has too many tables and seats and they lost the original vision of serving great italian food. Now they are forced to microwave everything to get it out of the kitchen. Shame shame shame. Won't be back. There are much better Italian restaurants in the area.

text: Can we get a 6th star for Ezras? Any eatery that makes food so delicious that I would consider changing my diet for is so deserving of a 6th star. I have been trying to rock the Paleo diet for over a year now however, with so many wonderful new dining options in Indy...and my love for beer... it's hard to stay true. Ezra's makes it easy..ier. It's one of a handful of places in Indy I personally feel I can go too, order from the menu, and not have to modify a meal. In addition, who knew Raw Vegan cuisine could be so delicious? I didn't. Every time I visit I tell myself if I could eat like this everyday I would go vegan. It is that good! Good news! They offer classes to learn more. Let's talk food shall we, this is what I have tried so far..... *Buddha Bowl (extremely filling, beets, honey spiced kale, fermented veggies, sunflower sprouts, avocado, tasty raw falafel balls, lemon Tahini dressing). So many wonderful flavors mixing together for an incredible mind blowing salad experience. *Nacho Mamma Bowl (warm beans & quinoa, greens, avocado, and that nacho cheeze! How do you make that cheeze? I want to know! Great dish and very filling. *RaWco Taco Salad (walnut taco meat & that nacho cheeze (again). Served with flax chips that work perfectly to scoop up that nacho cheeze. Best taco salad I have ever had hands down. This one is full of healthy goodness, you just feel good eating it. *Anti-inflammatory Turmeric Quinoa Salad (delicious and so good for you!) Perfect Grab N Go option to eat in between a meeting or a nice side dish. *Herbed Cashew Cheeze (tastes just like cheese but better). Great with flax crackers. I am thinking about adding it to future charcuterie boards for gatherings. Mondays they prep for the week so they only offer Grab N Go. Come early because items sell out quickly. Personal notes: I must try 1 of each of those amazing desserts in the case, the granola bowl, a hot tonic latte, and nourishing shots. Oh my! I have a lot of eating to do!

This is what a EXCELLENT Com Tam Thuan Kieu supposed to be & it exactly bring up the name of the word "Com Tam Thuan Kieu". text: Well worth the trip to uber out to Bacchanal from the hustle and bustle of Bourbon Street. The winery + restaurant feels like a summer music festival. You take the number and wait for your food to arrive. You can order drinks upstairs as well as downstairs. While we didn't luck out with outdoor seating, we did luck out with our food choices. The grilled whole fish was so buttery tender. Rather than preparing it in butter, it must have been prepared in quality olive oil because the olive scent was mesmerizing and really elevated the humble fish. The skin was a second away from being crispy, with all the fishiness gone. While I split this and the mussels with a friend, I could have easily had three whole fish prepared in this way. text: My one star rating is on tonights meal. We've gone to Island Way on many occasions and love the patio dining. This review is about tonights food. I ordered a fish which the waiter said I would love if I love sea bass. He told me it is cooked to medium rare. My waiter was attentive to my non-gluten needs. However, the fish arrived with very overdone and tough and tasteless. I sent it back ( rare for me) as it was so unenjoyable. Next I ordered the scallop appetizer. This seemed promising at first, with a nice sauce on the side. After a bite or two the extremely intense salt flavor set in. It was so salty I could barely taste the scallops. The salt was on the scallop, not the sauce. I rinsed one off in my water, but it was still too salty to eat. I gave one to my husband, who usually likes salty food, but he said it was an overwhelming amount of salt. We left one behind. Fortunately our salads were extra big tonight, as my meal consisted of two small scallops and a salad. Since I was hungry when I got there, I was anxious to leave so I could go home and eat, which I am now finally doing. I politely told the waiter the the scallops were awful and extremely over-salted. He was apologetic We were not charged for my main course which I sent back, just for my husbands rib eye ( which he found to be mediocre) and my scallops, and the ample salads. No manager came to check on what occurred. On the way home I called to speak to the manager to let her know I wasn't calling to get comped for anything, but wanted to give her the heads up that things were afoul tonight with the meals. She said she would speak to my waiter to see what happened, then call me back, but never did. We mostly like Island Way for the patio dining. The sides mostly have gluten, even the potatoes and the rice, which seems odd these days when so many other restaurants are more gluten aware and more caring of that dietary need. On other occasions the steaks have been excellent, but sometimes mediocre. The sea bass is sometimes excellent, sometimes over-cooked. You have to hit it right. I know we will return because the patio dining over the water is so relaxing. Too bad about the food.

text: Made an advance reservation one week out for my wife's 50th birthday celebration weekend. At the time of reservation I was showed a table, that the hostess recommended for our special night. We were seated on the main dining floor at a densely placed four top, right on top of another four top. Service started out great: knowledgeable descriptions of drinks, menu, etc. We began with cocktails and proceeded to order our entrees. After that, the service deteriorated. Let me back up. Ocean Prime uses a quasi team approach: server, expediter and bus/water person. Our salads arrived with only two of three guest receiving their salads. One person ordered salad only, so fair enough... I understand the timing. The entrees and "sides" were brought to our table by the expediter with no serving spoons for the sides or "duh" steaks knives for the filets. By this time, our server was busy attending to a large section of the main dining floor and had just been seated a booth with six people. Needless to say, we were not on his radar. There was an individual running drinks from the bar, but NO ONE ever checked back once our food was ordered. Really? This is serving 101 and for crying out loud, Applebee's knows that. Finally, the server's attention is grabbed, (should one really have to flag) as he passed by our table. My wife (Birthday Girl) is using her fork to serve the mashed potatoes side from a bowl. I mention to the server, as he is holding a tray with side dishes and serving spoons (for the booth of six next to us) that we did not receive serving spoons. He looks at the mashed potatoes and corn side and says, "Would you like a spoon?" Double duh! That was the first check back we had, customer initiated, well into our meal. Oh, our glasses of water are empty and the salad plates are clearly finished and remain unnoticed, sitting on the table. As the server made his way through the dining room, we flagged him a second time for water, literally begging for service. Here is the kicker, the server finally acknowledged the birthday occasion (The very reason we selected Ocean Prime) and said he would like to buy my wife a desert. My rub with this approach: 1 - Horrible service the entire night. 2 - Servers that have ignored you all night, then endear themselves at the end for gratuity sake. 3 - We literally waited 15 minutes for the "complimentary"creme brûlée once ordered Needless to say we had an awful experience on a very special and monumental birthday. Just to lend contrast,the preceding evening we went to Vetri. It was going to be a weekend celebration with Saturday at Vetri and Sunday at Ocean Prime. I just have to say, there could not have been a more stark contrast as to what "Great" looks like. On the way out of the restaurant I inquired as to when the GM would be back in? Suspecting something was wrong, the assistant manager (Where was she on the dining floor all night?) ask about our dining experience. I proceeded to let her know how our evening went or rather... did not. She offered free desert and the obligatory, "Come back and join us again and give us another chance" excuses and cop-outs. She lamented that Ocean Prime wants to deliver a 5 star experience and it is clear you did not get a 5 star experience. Triple duh...Really?? Big customer service tip: Make it right in the moment, because someone who has had such a poor experience does not want a free desert nor are they likely to take you up on your offer to return. My wife, who is the epitome of patience, even mentioned in her kind words, "How off the service was". Could not have been more disappointed in Ocean Prime. #oceanprime

text: We came during a Lightning game (Ferg's Live is right across the street from Amalie Arena) hoping to enjoy a fervent game-time crowd and atmosphere. We were relatively disappointed. Upon entering it was apparent that the concept was well-conceived but the execution still needs work. The outside area appears to be as much as four times the size as the indoor dining area, which is perfect since our climate allows outdoor dining most of the year. The TV's are well-placed and ubiquitous. While the sound for the Lightning game could be heard in the indoor part of the bar, management refused to put the sound on outside. To her credit, when we asked our bartender about the sound she went and checked with her manager and returned to give us the bad news. This would have been a minor annoyance, but the sound from the game came at the expense of loud, blaring techno music. It sounded like a club in Ybor, but scanning the crowd, I didn't see any 22-year-olds. The crowd was a nice mix of young professionals and sports fans in their 30's and 40's - so whom are they catering to and what crowd are they trying to attract? To be fair, I look for three things in a sports bar here in Tampa Bay: plenty of screens, plenty of OUTDOOR seating, and sound from the major sports attraction that is currently airing. Loud music AFTER the Lightning game might be a good marketing strategy to bring in the crowd spilling out of Amalie, but why does anyone presume I want to watch the Lightning game on mute or to a soundtrack that I would expect on 7th Avenue? The food is typical bar fare and the beer selections are unoriginal, which will appeal to the masses. I don't eat animal products, and to their credit, Ferg's did have a number of animal-free options. Despite the annoying atmosphere, which basically foiled our plan of enjoying the Lightning game, we ordered a couple of beers and sweet potato waffle fries. Unfortunately our bartender misunderstood our order and brought us what Ferg's calls "Sweet Baby Fries", which are sweet potato fries, but they are smothered in BBQ pulled pork, cheddar cheese, and diced onions. Our waitress was apologetic for the mistake and quickly put in the correct order. Nothing about the food was fast. Each order took over 15 minutes to come out. The correct ("plain") sweet potato fries were sprinkled with cinnamon-sugar and were relatively uninspiring. Our bartender's mistake and the speed of the food are minor inconveniences that I am willing to attribute to the growing pains of a new venture (they have only been open for a few weeks). We will try this place again in hopes that they will solve their identity crisis and offer a true sports bar atmosphere that is lacking in downtown Tampa. Note: if you are familiar with Ferg's in downtown St. Pete, the similarities end with the name. From what I have read, this is a venture of Jay Mize (Irish 31), who simply negotiated a deal to use the "Ferg's" name. It is not a "second location" or franchise.
label: NEG

text: Okay so I hate to break up the 5-star Yelp party going on for the newly opened Haven, however my recent experience (my birthday dinner) on March 23rd was... well, wrought with lack luster service and confusing menu explanations... overall we left with a feeling of "meh" and later headed somewhere else for a real entree. A few of my girlfriends went right after opening night and liked it, but warned that the menu was odd and they were having launch pains (totally expected)... damn the whole neighborhood has been waiting with baited breath to see what the popular "SideBerns" had evolved into during extensive renovations. We had 7PM reservations and pulled up to a disappointing $3 valet... I know, I know its Soho, but come on. Never mind, paid and was off to see the new gorgeous Haven interior. Very nice entrance - was greeted quickly by the hostess and escorted to a table in a what I thought was a very bright, noisy, dining room. I looked around squinting as it appeared the 8 ceiling spotlights (see pic) facing the bar area were set on high and super bright - glaring across the dining room. I noticed dim lit candles on shelves in the room that was reminiscent of a nice wine cellar. Exposed red brick, exposed beams in cathedral ceilings, a visible wine room behind the bar and cozy semi-circular round both against the walls. We sat in the middle with the light glaring down. It took about 5+ minutes for someone to finally stop by the table. We have a very quiet, soft-spoke waitress that seem disintested in the whole evening. She was nice enough - but not the caliber of professional, confident waiter you expect in a new restaurant of this caliber. We opened the folded paper menu and started looking at options. Keep in mind they have the SideBerns caliber wine menu also which was expected, but we opted for some craft cocktails. I asked for a Gimlet made with Titos vodka and shaken with a few slices of jalepeno. She came back and said no jalepeno - okay, darn - well just the Gimlet. It came back made with gin... when I asked her about the gin she said she had no idea what liquor was put into the drink. Lackluster - ugh. So far, not a very exciting birthday. She finally came back for our dinner order and we asked about the menu "explain how the top pages work, there are dozens of cheeses and meats listed. What does the headline on the page "Cheeses Five" mean? Is it a platter or something that has 5 cheeses? She said "what?" I repeated myself and she kind of apathetically said "cheeses are five dollars each. OHHH, I get it - so how big are the portions of cheeses? "very small" she said. Well, how many should we order for the table? "Depends on how hungry you all are?" What? It's an app right? What variety and amounts would YOU recommend for us so we have a nice tasting? "Well what kind do you like?". Oh my god. Just bring one of each category and let's add some pate. Can we have some bread too? "Well do you want to buy the bread service or do you want the little bread pieces that comes with the cheeses?" Um what is the difference? "One is a long piece of bread and the other are sliced. One costs $$, the other comes with the cheese." We'll take the free bread - LOL thanks. You get the drift of the confusion and ordering process that goes on? All this under those damn bright spotlights glaring off the table tops. No music playing - no ambience... BUT a pretty bar crowd! ;-) The cheese and meat platter came out and with some wine was fine. We should have left after that... but it's a birthday dinner so let's order entrees. I looked through the menu and we each ordered a dish. about 30 minutes later - dinner came out. Empty drinks and water glasses still sitting on the table... the plates were placed and I was surprised at how tiny the portions were. These mains are DEFINITELY small bites to be shared. We all nibbled and finished up - still hungry and unimpressed. There was conversation about ordering more food - Nope... we decided to pay up (after more than an hour in there) and head somewhere else for an impromtu "Part Two" of the dinner. We laughed and said my birthday would be a progressive dinner with us moving from location to location which actually turned a "meh" situation into something fun. Overall they have a long way to go. Create an ambience with lighting and music, pay more attention to the tables (drinks, water, etc), know the menu upside down - and backwards and be able to clearly recommend a meal (i.e. - would you like to stick to wines, cheeses and meats or enjoy a tasting of several main entrees - or both?). My advice to the management and team at Haven is smile, put some energy in your step and have some fun - it's a gorgeous new location, gorgeous crowd and the first customers coming in, are the folks that really want you all succeed and will be faithful. Will I go back? Yes, will return and give it a another chance.
label: NEG

text: This is one of my favorite hotels for business travel. The primary reason for this is the location. Not only is the Renaissance right by the airport, but it opens up right into the International Plaza and Bay Street. For those not familiar with Tampa, the International Plaza is a very upscale mall with stores such as Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, Gucci, Tory Burch, Henry Bendel, Tiffany, etc. Bay Street is an adjacent outdoor area with additional shops and tons of restaurants. This past week I worked at a convention at this Renaissance. I was able to fly in and take the shuttle to the hotel. I did not need to rent a car because everything I needed, including dining options, was at the hotel or next door at International Plaza. So convenient! The hotel itself is rather small for a Renaissance. At 8 floors and 287 rooms, the place actually has somewhat of a cozy feel to it. Guests actually congregate and socialize in the small lobby, hotel bar, and lovely courtyard. It is a great place for a small convention or meeting because participants can actually find each other. It had been a couple of years since I had stayed at this Renaissance. I was pleased to discover that the lobby and rooms had been renovated. The guest rooms themselves are not too large but very functional and comfortable. The room is certainly not big enough for leisure travel with my family of four, but it is fine for solo business travel or even for a couple. The room I had was spotless. Most important however is the bed, which was super comfy. Along with the crisp sheets, delicious duvet, and multitude of perfect pillows, I slept like a baby (something I don't normally do on a business trip). I did not need much from the staff but any interaction I had was extremely pleasant. The shuttle drivers were efficient. Late checkout? "No problem! When would you like it?" I ate at the restaurant, Pelagia, once during my stay. I just had a Salmon Salad but it was perfectly prepared. I do recall having yummy breakfasts there in the past. On, this visit I did eat breakfast in the concierge room once. The hot and cold items offered were impressive. The hotel does have a pool and a gym but unfortunately, I was too busy working to enjoy them. Funny, when I traveled to Tampa bimonthly in the past I did not stay here regularly and after this visit I was wondering why. Then my former colleague reminded me that their regular rates were a bit high (and we got better deals at the Hilton near by) . For this trip, I had a convention rate of $150/night - superndeal for a great hotel!

text: I live near this store and I'd been there a half dozen times over the years to get watch batteries changed. They also repaired a watch that was not running and had a broken band. The above tasks were successfully completed despite the fact that none of the people who work there are particularly nice. I weighed their personalities against the fact that they charged fair prices on repairs, performed these repairs while I waited and seemed to possess the necessary skills. As a general business rule I tend to favor performance and results over superficial traits, so was keen to continue bringing random jewelry repairs there. In early January 2015 I had an embarrassing and demoralizing experience at this store. After weeks of research I purchased a sapphire bracelet from Ross & Simons for my girlfriend as her Christmas gift. Within a day of wearing it one of the sapphires fell out. I was hoping it was a case of bad luck and was willing to have it inspected and repaired. Upon looking at it a man in his 50s or 60s came out from behind the counter and, with curt frustration, proceeded to tell me what a piece of junk the bracelet was and how badly I'd been ripped off. He must have used the word "junk" at least once in every sentence of his five-minute diatribe, and he spoke loudly enough that the other customers in the store heard everything. He showed me the stones up close in his jewelry magnifier and it was junk, sure enough. Obviously I returned the bracelet and got a full refund, but the money wasn't the point. I was sad enough about my failed gift, and his attitude was nothing but rudeness and arrogance. He made me feel like a second-class citizen and that is simply unacceptable. Just because you are an expert in your field doesn't give you the right to make someone feel like a complete loser should they require a piece of your precious knowledge. I'm never going back and you shouldn't bother going either, even if it is just for a simple watch battery replacement. Honestly, life is too short to involve yourself with people like these. What is it about this store that attracts this personality type? Finally, in case this is relevant to you, the overpriced items they sell look like tacky knickknacks from the 1960s.

text: I used to be a Golds gym member until recently when my membership finally expired. Now, don't get me wrong -- Golds is a nice gym. They also have a few hidden fees that no one seems to tell you about. One of them is the freeze fee. They will tell you when you sign up that you can freeze your account if not using it (summertime etc) but they will fail to tell you that there is a charge of apx $10. Yes...a CHARGE to not be there using the facility. Never have I experienced this at former gyms. The other thing is a form of an admin fee of apx $85 that gets mailed to you yearly. Again -- SURPRISE! Read your contract -- the BACK part, before you sign anything. Now on an interesting note - my contract expired just in time for Fit4Less to open up a mere stones throw from my home. $10/mo or $20 for the card that includes tanning and massage chairs. Well heck -- where do I sign up! I was a bit hesitant because I liked that Golds isn't overly busy. I called and asked one of the managers if he'd renew me for the higher amount of what I'd be paying at Fit4less (which would work out to apx $250/yr). He said no. text: http://www.wtsp.com/story/news/2015/11/11/ivory-mandarin-bistro-dunedin-restaurant-red-alert-roaches-toads/75617036/ DUNEDIN, Florida -- Debbie Abramson ordered a Chinese food delivery from Ivory Mandarin Bistro and says the peanut sauce chicken and vegetables dish called "I Don't Know" on the menu arrived with a questionable consistency. "I noticed the texture of the chicken, it was not normal," said Abramson. "In fact, it was worse than spongy and I knew something was wrong." She says it's not the first time she's had a bad experience at the restaurant. The Ivory Mandarin Bistro was closed after failing a health inspection. WTSP "I saw a roach by where I was sitting in a booth. And of course that was alarming. I don't like roaches." So Abramson asked 10 Investigates to check out the kitchen. State records show Ivory Mandarin Bistro was shut down as an emergency closure for two days beginning Sept. 10 with 27 violations after someone filed an anonymous complaint about grease icicles from the hood dripping into the woks. The complainant went on to say two softball-sized toads where underneath the wok burners feeding on an infestation of German cockroaches. A health inspector sent in to investigate the next day discovered live roaches and the accumulation of grease on food contact services and pooling on the ground. So 10 Investigates stopped in to check on conditions now two months later. Owner Puguh Sutahan was at first reluctant to allow our camera in the kitchen. "Today we have so many things going on, maybe we can do another time," said Sutahan when we first arrived. But after about an hour of waiting he eventually agreed to allow us inside. "I have no problem," he said. Inside, we immediately started spotting some repeat violations this restaurant was warned to correct on previous inspections. Among the issues, raw meat stored in the walk-in cooler in nonfood grade plastic to go bags, an open employee water bottle stored right on top. Employee personal items -- a hat, keys and cigarettes -- were stored in and around the bowls. And while we didn't see any toads, grease was still dripping down under the cooking equipment. "We do cleaning every day," said Sutahan. We also spotted evidence of remaining insect activity finding a dead roach on the floor in the middle of the kitchen. Under the ice machine we found a single live roach. It's no surprise -- roaches are attracted to grease and the standing water we found dripping underneath equipment. Plus the back kitchen door was wide open allowing vermin easy access inside. But perhaps most disturbing was what we found in the employee restroom right next to where food is made. There was no soap or paper towels for employees to wash their hands, usually considered a high-priority violation on official state health inspections. The owner asked employees to correct the issue right away. He says despite the issues we pointed out the restaurant's food is safe for customers. "It's pretty clean and the food is great," said Sutahan. And while Abramson has no idea what was wrong with her chicken, she's not impressed with Ivory Mandarin Bistro's history of recurring health code violations. "If they keep doing it they don't care," said Abramson. "It's wrong to let that continue." You can see Ivory Mandarin Bistro's complete inspection history here. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/inspectionDates.asp?SID=&id=6122936

text: Ugh, Sabrinas...you let me down so. After being told we had a 30 minute wait, we were seated 50 minutes later (so already I was irritable). This is a pet peeve of mine...if the wait is 50 minutes, just be honest! I understand sometimes it is difficult to judge, but when we requested there were 2 large parties in front of us and the hostess should have had a more realistic time frame! I was really underwhelmed by their menu. Most of their options I can cook myself ( really basic omlettes, pancakes..). Nothing stood out for me, particularly because I do not enjoy mexican food and quite a few of their dishes are mexican based. Additionally, their specials menu always confuses me. It seems like they take everything going bad in the kitchen and throw it on a plate. I am talking like pancakes with fried eggs, chorizo sauce, papaya and peppers all on one "scramble"...sounds more like my garbage disposal than a breakfast special! I setteld on Blueberry Pancakes but I was denied. The kitchen had run out of blueberries, sigh. Not willing to spend $12-15 dollars on an egg dish I can easily make in my own home, I got Banana Chocolate Chip (short stack) pancakes instead. They were really underwhelming. Firstly, the fact that they were a short stack is laughable. These were two huge pancakes, and I could not finish them. Secondly, the pancakes were dry and bland, practically crumbly. I am not an expert, but it was certainly not what you would expect from a well-known breakfast joint. Sabrinas, I will not be returning. Your long waits, weird menu and overpriced breakfast junk doesn't appeal to me. I will be taking my brunching elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: I was raised in south Louisiana and live in Nola. I rarely eat at these types of places in the quarter since there are so many other authentic dishes to be found outside of the quarter. However, my tourist friends preferred to eat in the quarter so I chose this place based on the reviews. In short, I was embarrassed. One friend ordered the "award winning crab cakes". I'd love to know what contest awarded them because they were NOT seasoned. Two other friends ordered poboys. I've never seen a poboy this tiny, nor barely dressed. I ordered the Greek salad with grilled shrimp. The shrimp were bland and this salad they call "Greek" was simply lettuce, two slices of tomato, and two slices of onion . NOT a Greek salad in my book. And it filled up MAYBE 1/3 of the bowl it was in. As my friends ate, I waited 3 minutes to get some salad dressing before I had to get up and ask for some. Come one people give me a break. I left hungry. I was hesitant to eat at a place like this in the quarter, and now I know never to do that again. I'll be sure to take my friends out of that tourist trap where they don't know what southern cooking is, to a neighborhood place like uptown, mid-city, or the Bywater for some REAL damn food. Or I'll just cook it myself. As for the service, it was ok. Nothing to write home about. If it weren't for the average service, I'd give one star.
label: NEG

text: Nope. Not going back. There are plenty of other good car washes in the area. I could probably look past their aging facility and not particularly friendly employees- it's a car wash, after all. However, after they washed my car, the electronic hatch opener on my new Highlander wasn't operative. It was definitely working before the wash. I filled out a damage report and was told the owner would contact me. He never did. To be fair, I eventually figured it out (someone may have messed with the electronic key), and as far as I know, no damage was done to the car (other than perhaps by their repeated attempts to manually open and close it). But the least they could have done was follow-up, offer a free wash, or something other restitution for my time and trouble. It seems that there could be two reasons I never heard back. 1) The owner was afraid he would have to pay to have my car fixed; or 2) the employee who filled out the damage form didn't follow up. I find the second one hard to believe- the cashier filled out the form, and told me that she was going to call the owner that afternoon. Either way, it shows a pretty big void in their customer service process, at least as to my own situation. My car is new and I spent a lot of money on it. I would hate to think how they would respond if they scratched the car or did other damage. The whole point of a customer service business is to give excellent customer service. Certainly, the quality of the work is important. But what distinguishes a good car wash, say, for example, Miles Auto Wash in Franklin, from a mediocre to bad one, is the people who work there. If you don't believe me, then try both places and write your own review.
